short: A British Royal Navy research vessel commanded by James Cook on his first voyage of discovery.
full:
Originally built as a sturdy coal-carrying vessel named the Earl of Pembroke, the ship was purchased by the Royal Navy in 1768 and renamed HMS Endeavour. Her broad, flat-bottomed design made her ideal for navigating shallow waters and carrying extensive provisions. Commanded by Lieutenant James Cook, she embarked on an ambitious voyage to the Pacific Ocean.

The expedition successfully observed the 1769 transit of Venus from Tahiti before charting New Zealand and the eastern coast of Australia. Narrowly surviving a grounding on the Great Barrier Reef, the Endeavour returned to England in 1771. She was later sold out of naval service and eventually scuttled in Rhode Island during the American Revolutionary War.
